PR #258 is finished and marked ready. The pushed head is `e23cf5fe88`. CI has not run on it yet, since this session pushed it.

**Why attempt 1 didn't finish:** the fix (`cdce86db63`) was committed locally but never pushed. NOTES was still untracked with a placeholder for results, and the mutant and falsification runs had not been done. So the CI GREEN in the resume brief was on the claim commit and says nothing about the fix. This is recorded in `docs/lanes/handbackstrand/NOTES.md`.

**What this attempt did:**
- Committed NOTES, merged `origin/master` (35 commits, no conflicts) and pushed.
- Ran the new test file `99-handback-strand.sh` on its own in a scratch worktree at `origin/master`. The handback.sh file was never swapped in place, nothing in that worktree was staged, and I removed it afterwards:

  | handback.sh under test | Result |
  |---|---|
  | Old code on master (falsification) | 13 checks fail, including (b): the old code resumes the lane on a new head |
  | Mutant 1: key the arm marker on the head again | 13 fail, (b) fails |
  | Mutant 2: drop the in-flight check | 7 fail, all of them in (d) |
  | This branch | 98 pass, 0 fail |

- The full `selftest.sh` gives 1365 passed, 0 failed.
- `preflight.sh` passed, including the territory and coverage checks.
- Rewrote the PR body over REST and read it back. Its `Files:` line matches `git diff --stat origin/master...HEAD`, and it says `Prediction: none` because there is no device run.

**One behaviour to check at review:** the in-flight hold also applies to the quiet-clock cause, not just the arm cause. My reasoning is that a lane whose arm is still queued is waiting, not stranded. NOTES says so.
